Mydei's first mission in ages turns out to be kind of a mess. Cipher wakes him up at four-thirty in the morning, and he isn't expecting it. He isn't taken on missions often. The last time was at least a month or two ago, and even then he only sat in the getaway car. Just in case, Anaxa told him. You're here just in case they need you. But they didn't. They’re a capable bunch, and they rarely do.

He doesn't have super strength like Phainon or enhanced senses like Aglaea or Cipher's short-ranged teleportation. You have more… specific applications, Cipher likes to tell him, You’re our trump card. Every good heist needs a trump card!

And Mydei gets it, he does. He's life or death in the situations where he's actually needed. It doesn't make sense to send him up against powers he can't counteract. Mydei is trained in combat, sure, and is damn good at it, but up against someone with strength like Phainon or speed or elemental abilities or something else along those lines, he's at a dangerous disadvantage. Not helpless, but not the best choice for the job either. So they keep him back even if it pisses him off, and he gets it, he does.

Today, though, is different. Today is one of the rare days when Mydei gets to be useful. Cipher shakes him awake from a restless sleep, her expression a bit manic and overexcited. Mydei sits up and gets this nervous thrill. Stage fright and anticipation at once. Even if he's been training forever, his experience out on the field is still considerably limited.

"Aglaea's fine," is the first thing Cipher says. The whole point of the original mission was to rescue her from the Cleaners. They left late last night, leaving Mydei to stay back and try to sleep. He was too pissed and anxious to get anywhere, though, and now he's here. Needed.

"We got her back," Cipher continues, voice hushed and secretive even though there's no one here to listen in. They check their flat for taps every other week. "it's just..."

Mydei pushes his blanket off. "Just...?"

"You'll see," Cipher says, grinning. "I called Anaxa and he’s got the car. Bring your shit. We need to get everyone out of there before they can catch us."

Mydei grabs for the bag where he keeps his gear for easy access and follows Cipher out in socks and his pajama pants, taking the elevator down to the ground floor. The car is idling out front, Anaxa looking bored in the driver's seat. Mydei climbs in the back, Cipher takes passenger.

"Explain," Mydei prompts, digging his undershirt out of the bag. It's black, skintight and long-sleeved, and he struggles into it, switching his pants for a pair lined with pockets and a holster to secure his handgun. Anaxa pulls away from the curb, and Cipher folds her arms around the back of her seat to look at him, her hood falling over her eyes before she lifts it, eyes glinting ominously.

"We found Aglaea is the shipping yard like Tribbie expected," she says, "but we had to look through an awful lot of containers to find her…” Her canines glint. “There was another girl in one of them. She's…”

"Dangerous," Anaxa cuts in gruffly.

"Scared," Cipher says instead. "She's tied up and drugged as much as Aglaea is, but she wouldn't let anyone come close. She kept saying she was going to hurt us."

"Dangerous," Anaxa says again. The car goes over a bump. Mydei catches himself on Cipher's seat, quickly doing up the buckles on his body armor.

"You weren't there, Professor," Cipher argues. "You didn't see her. She wasn’t threatening us, she was genuinely terrified… Boy do I love a good mystery like this one.” She turns to Mydei behind her again, tail beating against the seat. "We tried to take her with us, but Phainon got burned when he touched her.”

Something twists in Mydei’s gut. “That dumb fuck,” he curses. “Is he okay?”

“Fine, assuming we can get them out on time,” Anaxa tells him. “But the girl is dangerous. Taking this lightly would be folly.”

"She kept telling us not to come closer,” Cipher says drily. “It’s not like she was trying to hurt him. That Deliverer kid is just dumb.”

Anaxa is silent. Mydei shoves his hands into his gloves and digs his boots out of his bag last. His stomach flips and flips and flips. Strife, all the time they’ve made him sit on the sidelines must have turned him into a coward. "And that's where I come in," he says.

"Yeah," Cipher agrees, tipping her head over the back of the seat to look at him now, ears twitching. She isn’t wearing her seatbelt, and Anaxa is scowling. Another feline grin, twin finger guns pointed his way. “Trump card.”

chapters.title: Chapter 1
chapters.html:
Mydei takes a breath and secures his gun to his waistband. "Wonderful," he says, loading up his pockets with the essentials. Phainon burnt, Aglaea drugged up, some strange girl begging them to stay away. What happened with this mission? Things never go awry like this with Aglaea leading them. Her capture screwed them all over. When he's done gearing up, he settles back and finally buckles his seat belt. Anaxa speeds at least twenty miles over the limit.

"You've got this," Cipher tells him, still holding up the finger guns. She doesn’t act like it, but she’s older, and she's been on so many more missions than Mydei has. She and Aglaea were a duo before they picked the rest of them up like strays. Aglaea was the brains, Cipher did the dirty work.

Mydei has maybe a dozen missions to his name but they seem to have full faith in him. That, or they’re just desperate. Either way, he manages an expression that’s much more confident than he feels and says, “Of course I do.”

The shipping yard is just a sea of cargo containers and more cargo containers. Anaxa can't drop them off too close for fear of attracting attention, so Cipher leads the way as they walk, checking in on her in-ear.

"They're still secure," she murmurs after a moment, keeping a close eye on their surroundings. "Phainon says Aglaea can hear us."

"Isn’t she drugged?" Mydei asks, feeling the crunch of gravel under his boots, starting to remember what the mission scene feels like. Settling in, better than he’d worried he would. It’s always like that. He’s a quick adapter. He has to be, after everything he’s been through.

“Yeah,” Cipher replies, but offers no further explanation. A little further, she knocks thrice on the door to one of the shipping containers. It creaks open, and there's Phainon and Aglaea inside. Phainon is in gear, all tight black from head to toe, straps and buckles securing everything in place. His expression is far more severe than Mydei is used to seeing. Nothing like the eager golden retriever he is when he comes home after a successful mission. Not quite the stubborn determination of a spar either. No, he’s serious now, brows set, gaze dark. A smear of dirt on his cheek, hair a mess. Looking at him brings back the odd flipping in Mydei’s stomach.

They haven’t had a chance to talk much. Not since things got weird. Not since things got real. He hears Phainon’s inhale, and then he tears his gaze away.

Aglaea looks a bit worse for wear, her dress dirtied and torn at the hems. There are bruises on her cheekbone, scratches and scabs on her shoulders and arms. Her pupils are dilated wide enough to swallow her irises, but Mydei knows she can’t see a thing, not the way the rest of them can. She isn’t speaking, and he gets the sense that anything she might say will be cryptic and strange.

"She's two containers over," Phainon murmurs, ushering them in. His fingers have been hastily bandaged, Mydei notices. Burned, but not irreversibly, from touching this girl. Quietly, he slips around the door, circling Mydei’s arm with his good hand. His touch is cold, softly squeezing. Alive, Mydei thinks, gaze glued to him. He’s fine, but they’re on a mission, and nothing else he’s been worrying about is important in the meantime. Phainon turns to the other two. "Cipher, stay with Aglaea. Get her out of here if something happens. Mydei, let’s go.”

They slip out of the shipping container, shutting the door behind them as soundlessly as they’re able. “Deliverer,” Mydei whispers.

Phainon only looks at him for a moment, gaze flicking between his eyes before he turns away. “Later,” he says, lightly pulling Mydei along. His grip loosens and slips off. Mydei catches his hand, squeezes it, waits for the edge of his smile in the night. We’re okay, it says. Don’t worry about that much right now.

The nerves come back as Phainon leads the way, softly padding through gravel, carefully checking every which way.

The door to the right shipping container is chained shut, and Phainon quickly undoes it, the links clattering, ginger with his hurt fingers. "She's scared," he says quietly. "Drugged worse than Aglaea. We need to keep her calm if we’re going to get her out, or she’ll just alert the Cleaners."

"She hurt you,” Mydei notes.

"Not badly," Phainon says, holding up his hand. The bandages on his fingertips are stained gold with his blood, but he smiles. “If something like this was enough to bench me, I’d hardly be worthy of being your equal.”

It’s still not entirely clear what happened to him, what exactly this girl did. They wouldn’t have brought Mydei out if it were elemental magic or some kind of attack. So what is this, what is she? "Why didn't you just bring Aglaea back and get treated? Why wait for me to come out?" Mydei asks.

"It’s faster to send Cipher than to make Tribbie drive here and back,” Phainon says simply, setting the chains down as quietly as he can. He turns to Mydei with this strong gaze, and Titans, he cares about too much, doesn’t he? The weight of the world stubbornly on his shoulders, like he thinks it makes him some hero to cling to everyone’s hopes but his own. "We're bringing her back," he says firmly.

“What’s so special about her?” Mydei asks, frustrated, almost. Because Phainon is hurt, because this is the only mission he’s been sent on in months, and he doesn’t even know what he’s here for. They could have left, nothing to it. Why does this matter?

“We’re all strays, Mydeimos,” Phainon says softly, taking Mydei’s hand again and pulling it to his mouth. “She needs help, same as the rest of us did at one point or another. Please.”

Mydei doesn't have the full story. He only knows what he's been told, which is barely anything at all, but maybe that’s all there is to know right now. He can't comprehend why Phainon might feel this strongly about bringing back someone who could very well be an enemy, but... He’s sure, and Mydei trusts him with everything. Even Cipher seems half invested in taking this girl home. He sucks in a breath and nods. Phainon nods back and drops his hand.

"Take her to Anaxa’s car. The rest of us will go with Tribbie."

"Alright," Mydei says, setting a hand on the door handle. Phainon steps back, edging into the shadows. "You're not coming?"

"I'll be out here," he says, reaching to rub his neck. "She keeps crying when she sees me."

"Oh."

An awkward smile, an awkward laugh. There he is, in the flesh. Mydei could be sick with it, sick with him. "Yeah."

Slowly, Mydei pulls the door open. There's a flashlight in one of his pockets. He pulls it out and clicks it on before he ducks inside, pulling the door half-closed behind him. A girl with hair long enough to pool on the floor where she sits and golden blood on her ragged white dress winces against the brightness and shrinks into the corner. Her hands and knees are bound, and she looks a hundred times worse than Aglaea does. Worse for wear. Terrified. Hungry.

A stray, like the rest of them. Mydei takes one look at her and gets it. Maybe he’s not the most selfless and compassionate of their bunch, but he gets it.

He wonders where she came from, why she's here. Was she kidnapped like Aglaea was? He steps a little closer.

"No," the girl rasps, pulling her knees in. Her voice is rough, like she's been crying. Mydei can't see her face very well, just the point of her chin and her dry, cracked lips. Her bare feet on the cold, hard metal of the shipping container. "Don't," she says when Mydei takes another step. She sounds so scared. "I'll hurt you like I hurt your friend."

Slowly, Mydei sits down a few feet away from her, and she squeezes far enough into the wall to move farther from him that it must hurt. Her whole body must ache from the binds and her position. Mydei isn't so nervous anymore. His throat clicks as he swallows. "What's your power?" he asks. "Fire control? Or... heat? Something like that?"

Silence. The girl's eyes are closed. She’s shaking. After a long moment, she asks, "Are you going to kill me?"

Mydei doesn't know what to say to that. "No," he offers, and Titans, he gets it now. A lot of them start out like this. Lost and abused and afraid. Mydei started out like this too, half-drowned and unable to trust a soul after his own father threw him into the sea. "No one's going to hurt you," he promises.

A beat. The girl's eyes peel open, dazed and dilated, considering, and then they close again. "You're going to kill me," she says like she's sure of it. "I'm okay with it." She's got narrow, sloped shoulders, a head that hangs down like she has something to be ashamed of, choppy bangs obscuring her face. She seems so sad. More than scared, she just seems sad, tired of whatever kind of life she’s been forced to live.

"No one's going to kill you," Mydei insists. Blood on her dress, but not a single scratch on her. Where Aglaea had been scraped and bruised, this girl's skin is pale and untouched. Closer, there’s a print on her shoulder... fingers, maybe. Phainon's, from when he grabbed her and got hurt. Is it just her skin, then? Her touch?

"What's your name?" Mydei tries to ask instead.

The girl lifts her head. Her hair is a mess, tangled and matted, but a soft, pale pink color. Her eyes are big and wary. She looks so dazed and exhausted, but more resigned than scared now. Like she really thinks Mydei is going to kill her. Like she really is okay with that. "Castorice," she finally says.

"Castorice," Mydei repeats. "I'm Mydei."

"Okay."

"Could you tell me about your power?"

She looks at him blankly. "I hurt everyone I touch," she says, the words stringing together a bit, wavering at the edges.

Likely nothing elemental, then. Mydei sucks in a breath. "Could I untie you?" he asks.

"You'll touch me," she says. There's a long pause. "You'll get hurt."

She's in a long dress and gloves tall enough to cover her wrists beneath the bonds. "Even through your clothes?" Mydei asks. A silent nod. Mydei watches her for a moment. He thinks about Phainon's bandaged fingers, his insistence that this girl come with them. "Okay," he says, lifting a hand. "Can I test something?"

Castorice shrinks back even further, if that's possible. The way she does it is slow, kind of delayed. Mydei has no idea how long she's been here. She must need food and water to get the drugs out of her system, but she's clearly weak and dehydrated. Mydei needs to get her out of here quickly.

"No," Castorice slurs. "Don't— Don't touch, you'll hurt... I'll hurt you."

"Other people’s powers don’t affect me," Mydei tries. Or, many don’t. He never knows which ones until he comes into contact with them. Hence why he rarely goes on missions. He's a last ditch effort in an emergency. "Yours won’t either." Or he'll end up with fried fingers like Phainon's, but he'll survive. It'll hurt, but he'll survive. "Can I try?"

"Don’t, please."

Mydei grits his teeth. Be calm, he tells himself. Yelling won’t help, his fists won’t help. He’s too used to solving problems by force. Habits are hard to break. Be gentle. But his patience is running thin, and their time is running out. "So... What's your plan, then? Just staying here forever? Hanging out all tied up until the bad guys come back for you? Or did they really just leave you here to die?"

Castorice's face changes at that. She looks scared again. Mydei wonders so many things about her. He has more questions than answers. She swallows thickly. "How do you know I'm not one of them?" she asks, strangely sober.

"You're tied up and trapped in a shipping container," Mydei points out, drier than he intends. “Why would you be one of them?”

Castorice opens her mouth, closes it again. Her head falls back into the wall. She's still making herself so small it must be painful. "Different bad guys, then."

Mydei considers that, has been considering that. "You don't want to hurt me or my friends," he says finally. "Bad guys usually want to hurt people."

A beat. Two, three. Phainon waits outside, just a breath away in case something happens. Aglaea might be listening, a couple containers over, if she’s well enough for it. Someone would say something if there was a problem. They still have time, but he has no idea how much. He’s good with head-on confrontations, not time limits and hiding.

Castorice looks at him, gaze foggy. She's dangerous, but she seems safe. She hurt Phainon. She could hurt Mydei too, but she might not. She wouldn’t mean to if she did. Either way, they need to get her out of here as quickly as possible. Mydei doesn't know her story, but he agrees with the rest. They can't leave her here.

And titans, he doesn't want to. For some reason he cares—if only a little bit —like Phainon and Cipher do. A breath. There's only one way to find out if Mydei will be immune to her power or not. Quickly, he taps Castorice on the leg. It makes her flinch like she'd been stabbed instead of poked, but there’s no pain on Mydei’s end, no blood, no injured fingers.

"No," Castorice says anyway. "No, no, why would you—"

"I'm not hurt," Mydei tells her, displaying his hand. It’s gloved, so it doesn’t prove much. Castorice presses herself as far away from him as she can get, tucking her limbs out of the way as best as she can. Mydei almost feels guilty. He scoots back to give her more space.

"Castorice," he says, trying to be patient. "You didn't hurt me."

"I—" At this, Castorice squints, face scrunching up like her head hurts trying to comprehend that.

Slowly, Mydei pulls off his gloves and displays his hands again, entirely unscathed. "Look," he says, and after a confused moment, Castorice does. "I didn't lie; your power doesn’t work on me."

"You..." She’s staring. Slowly, awkwardly with her arms bound behind her back, she peels away from the wall so she can see better in the terrible lighting. "You aren’t… hurt?"

"No," Mydei says, offering a sharp smile. "Can I untie you now?"

Castorice's gaze flicks up to his face. She thinks about it for a long while, but Mydei doesn't push. He waits until gingerly, Castorice pushes her legs in his direction. "Don't touch," she says, wincing away before Mydei's hands can even come close. She braces herself for it, and Mydei wonders how old she was when her power presented itself. How many people she's hurt with her touch to be so afraid of it. He’s careful to avoid her skin as he unties her.

"Will you come with us?" he asks, pulling the rope about Castorice's ankles free. "I promise no one will kill you."

She shifts so Mydei can get her wrists, stiffens when Mydei accidentally brushes against her gloves. So scared of it. So unused to it. Mydei didn't even touch her properly.

"Your friend," Castorice starts, fingers twitching. "I hurt him."

"Phainon's fine," Mydei tells her, "bandaged up and everything already. You could hit him with a truck and he’d get up after." Quiet. Castorice's wrists go free, and she pulls them into herself, massaging their aches. "He's dumb, huh? Should have listened when you told him not to touch."

Castorice doesn't nod, like she's afraid of agreeing. Like she thinks it's her fault, even if Phainon is the dumbass who didn't listen. Mydei should stop thinking so much. "We want you to come with us," he says. "Help get the drugs out of your system and give you a place to sleep for the night, at least."

She watches him, quietly considering, and then nods. "For the night," she echoes.

"Longer, if you want," Mydei says as gently as he can muster. "You don't have to stay, but you can."

"Okay," Castorice says warily. She looks like he wants to trust Mydei but isn't sure if she can. That's fair. They're strangers. Mydei had taken a long time to learn to trust again too. He’d fought tooth and nail before even considering joining the rest of the Chrysos Heirs. Phainon was the one who convinced him, pinning him down and winning their first fight only because Mydei had been malnourished and unrested. He’d held Mydei’s wrists to his chest, blood dripping from a cut on his forehead into Mydei’s face, and he’d had to say it over and over. We’re not going to hurt you, can’t you see that? I could kill you right now, but I’m not? Why do you think that is? Why, Mydeimos?

That was before either of them had grown into their powers. Titans, it feels like so long ago now.

"Okay," Mydei repeats, standing up. He offers a hand, but Castorice doesn't take it, pushing herself up on unsteady legs. She wobbles, drugged and sore and exhausted, and Mydei fights the urge to catch her or to offer help.

She stumbles into the wall, knees failing her, and this time Mydei does have to catch her before she can crash to the ground again. She's small and narrow and too thin in Mydei's arms, and for a moment she just goes still, staring up with these wide, bloodshot eyes. And then she struggles, fighting to get away and crying, "Don't, don't, don't," over and over again, shaking, curling in on herself on the floor, and Mydei feels sick watching her. They all come beaten and bruised before they heal, but this—

"Castorice," Mydei says. Again, firmer, hearing the blood in his ears, "Castorice." He crouches. "You didn't hurt me. Look. Look. I'm okay. You need to—”

The door creaks open. "We need to go," Phainon says. "Right now. The Cleaners are coming."

"Shit," Mydei says. "Shit, shit."

"Are you immune?" Phainon asks, glancing at Castorice, this look in his eyes. He's urgent, but he isn't afraid. He trusts Mydei wholeheartedly the same way Mydei trusts him. Mydei nods once. "Then grab her and let's go."

"Shit," Mydei says again. He crouches, willing his heart to calm down long enough for him to figure this out. Castorice has gone quiet, but Mydei knows she can't walk by herself, as drugged as she is. She's just curled up, making herself so small, as far from Mydei as she can get. "Castorice," he says, a little softer. Level, comforting, safe. None of these things come naturally, but he can't flip out on her right now. "You haven't hurt me, okay? You won't." She doesn't respond, just shakes her head, shrinking away when Mydei tries to approach. "I need to help you," Mydei tells her. Cipher and Aglaea have joined Phainon in the doorway. Urgent, all of them. Again, "You're not going to hurt me."

Mydei reaches out. "No," Castorice protests weakly. Mydei hesitates, gritting his teeth, but he doesn’t even have a moment to think before Cipher is putting a hand on his shoulder and brushing past him, pulling something from the inside of her cloak.

“Don’t take it personal, princess,” she says, ignoring the way Castorice shrinks back to press something into her neck, careful not to touch her. A sedative. Castorice barely mutters a few more weak protests before her energy slips away from her and she goes limp.

“Cipher,” Phainon says, voice low.

“It needed to happen, Deliverer, unless you were planning on letting her scream and cry and alert every Cleaner within a mile,” she says, pulling the syringe free and backing away. She turns to Mydei. “All yours. Let’s go.”

“We’re not kidnappers,” Phainon starts. Aglaea is the one who hushes them before they can continue arguing, still out of it.

“They see us,” she says, and her voice is frighteningly clear, slightly accented, though her eyes are still crazed and clouded. “I hear… ‘Chrysos,’ they’re saying. ‘Maiden of war.’”

Strange and cryptic, unsettling. Aglaea always reacts strangely when drugged. Her senses are already far different from anyone else’s, alter them on top of that and you get this.

Mydei quits hesitating and hauls the unconscious Castorice onto his back, pulling her arms around his neck, grabbing her under the thighs. She’s completely limp, light as a feather, breathing shallow against the back of his neck. She’s barely even warm, Titans above. Mydei gets her off the ground with ease.

Phainon wraps an arm around the delirious Aglaea to support her, and the five of them head out of the shipping container, slipping into its shadows to regroup. A quick scan of the area reveals nothing. Mydei turns to Aglaea. "How much time do we have?"

"They're watching," she says. “I feel it. They see… ‘Goldweaver,’ ‘Maiden of War.’ One minute. No, less. Seconds. They’re close, closer now.” She isn’t walking well, and her eyes squint, mouth pressing into a hard line. What does the world look like to her? What does it feel like? Her threads can spread for miles, passing sound and sensation to her, but right now she’s so high nothing must make sense to her. Phainon just picks her up and slings her over his shoulder like a sack of potatoes, easy like she weighs nothing at all. He can lift a car one handed, since his strength manifested.

"Okaaay," Cipher says. "Move out, team. Quickly, yeah? I’d like to bask in victory tonight.”

Castorice still doesn’t stir. It barely feels like she’s breathing. There are too many drugs in her system. They need to get her to Hyacine, fast.

The ground is some odd combination of dirt, sand, and gravel, and it crunches with every step. "Thirty seconds,” Aglaea says, jostling with every step Phainon takes. Her arms dangle downward, fingers outstretched, tangled in faintly glowing gold threads. “They’re close now, everywhere, all sides. ‘Servant of Death, must—’”

"All sides?" Cipher hisses.

"I think," Aglaea continues, "they see us. They’re looking me in the eyes." Nevermind that her eyes are directed toward nothing but Phainon’s ass.

A breath passes. They’re all dead silent. Gravel crunches, and then there's a shout from behind. "Run," Cipher says, voice low, tail puffing up, and they do. All hell breaks loose. Mydei does his best to hold Castorice as stable as he can as he runs for his life. It's dark and he can hardly see where he's putting his feet, but he doesn't slow down. Phainon runs at his side, keeping pace. They exchange a glance, a grin as the adrenaline starts to kick in.

"Help us out, Aglaea," Phainon pants. Footfalls behind them, more shouting, metal creaking. The shipping yard is like a labyrinth; the Cleaners aren’t looking in the right places.

"It's dark," Aglaea murmurs. Castorice starts to slip, so Mydei adjusts his grip under her legs, tangling in the bunched fabric of her dress. "There are rocks. So many rocks. They’re looking at me."

"Very helpful," Phainon laughs. “What else?”

"Give her to me," Cipher says. "I'll get her to Tribbie." They're close to the cars, or that wouldn't work. Cipher's range is pretty short alone, half that with someone else. She can go maybe 50 meters per jump with Aglaea. Still, it's faster than running. Phainon practically tosses Aglaea to her, and then she's gone.

"I've got your back," Phainon tells him with a grin, barely even panting, pulling out his handgun. Anaxa and Tribbie's cars aren't parked in the same spot. They'll part ways here. Phainon won't stall too much, but he'll buy them a little time. “Let’s see who can get out of here faster, yeah?” The glimmer in his eye, the promise. Every mission Mydei has even been on, Phainon has had his back. There’s no one else he would trust it to.

He hoists Castorice a little higher and tries to catch his breath. "You’re on, Deliverer.” He can see light. A pair of figures break out from between a few shipping containers.

Phainon grins. "See you on the other side," he laughs. A gunshot. Mydei's ears ring. They split off in opposite directions, Phainon toward the Cleaners, Mydei toward Anaxa’s car. He can see it, a few hundred meters away. Phainon will get to Tribbie safely. He always does. Another gunshot. Mydei kind of wants to laugh. He’s fucked up on adrenaline.

“I’ve got you,” he says under his breath, more to himself than the unconscious Castorice. His muscles are burning. She’s starting to slip again. Ten more steps, the backseat door to the car rolls open. Another gunshot, farther away. They’re after Phainon, as planned. Mydei practically throws himself and Castorice inside, awkwardly landing face-first as the door closes behind him. Anaxa starts driving before Mydei can even sit up.

Wincing, Mydei eases Castorice off his back and upright, leaning her against the car door and buckling her in. Her eyes stay shut. She keeps breathing. More gunshots in the background. Mydei's heart does nothing to calm itself, still thundering in his ears as he does his own seatbelt. The ride is a far cry from smooth.

"I’m in touch with Tribios," Anaxa calls. "She has the rest of the team. They're being tailed."

Mydei lets out a breath. "Do what you need to," he says, and Anaxa pulls off onto a side road.

"Keep an eye on the back," Anaxa instructs. Mydei turns in his seat, freeing his handgun from his waistband. He keeps an eye out on Anaxa’s blind side as well, squinting in the dark. "That kid buckled in good?"

A glance at Castorice, still sleeping. "Yeah," Mydei confirms. Gunshots. Three of them. The car vibrates under Mydei's feet.

"I see them," Anaxa says, the engine revving as he speeds up. The car wrenches into a turn, Mydei grabbing onto the back of the seat. Anaxa says something to Tribbie through his in-ear, then addresses Mydei, "We're good behind?"

"All clear," Mydei says.

"All clear," Anaxa repeats to Tribbie. "Send her over."

More gunfire. Cipher blinks into the passenger's seat of the car. "Shit," she says, “it isn’t easy teleporting into a moving vehicle, you know. How fast are you going? A hundred fifty? You guys are lucky I’m as fleet-footed as I am."

Anaxa checks the speedometer. "Ninety-three," he answers drily. "All you, kid."

"There are three cars," Cipher says in a rush, "get one away from Tribbie, and then get me close. You'll have to be fast."

"One's already following us," Mydei says. There's someone leaning out the window, a rifle aimed in their direction. "They’ve got a gun." Anaxa slows down just a little, letting them catch up.

Cipher turns to look, tongue between her teeth, eyes narrow. "A little closer," she says, ears perking atop her head. Two gunshots. One hits the car, clanging against metal. "Closer…” There’s a click as Cipher turns the safety off her gun. "Perfect. Don't get too far." And then she's gone. Four more shots. The car behind them swerves and drives into a ditch. Cipher blinks back into the car, sighing for show, tail swishing. "One shot left," she says, waving a hand at Mydei. "Help a cat out, would you?" Mydei passes his gun over, watches her fingers curl tight over it, nails painted black, knuckles white. She’s good at pretending, but she’s scared too.

Anaxa steps on the gas to catch up to Tribbie. The other two cars won't leave her alone, shots popping in the space between them.

"Just get me close," Cipher says, her eyes crazed. "We can’t lead them away. Just... get me close, and I'll take care of everything."

"Cipher," Anaxa says, voice low.

"I've done this before," she says, bending over the back of his seat to give Mydei another upside-down smile. There's blood on her cheek. Red, not her own. "I'm a professional."

"Go for the left one," Anaxa says, gaining on the two Cleaner cars. "And do try to keep the mess out of the road."

"Got it, Prof," Cipher says. One more smile. "Stay close."

"Got it."

"See y’all in a minute."

Cipher teleports away. Mydei's stomach twists up into knots. He can't see much of anything. He can only hear the gunshots and the crash and feel the way Anaxa swerves hard enough to slam him into the door.

She’s supposed to teleport before the crash happens. She takes control of one car and crashes it into the second, but she gets out at the last second so she doesn't get hurt. That’s what’s supposed to happen. But Mydei heard the crash and she isn't here and when he squints out the window, he can see the two cars, collided and crushed like tin cans, sparking with flame and smoke, but he can’t see her.

"Shit," he says, stomach dropping. "Shit. Where is she?”

The tires scream as Anaxa brakes, wrenching the car into a u-turn. "She's fine," he says. "Relax. She missed, that's it. She couldn't make it into the car. Keep an eye out for her."

So he keeps an eye out as they circle back to the wreckage of the Cleaner cars. No more gunshots follow. Tribbie’s car has made it out, but where’s Cipher?

They drive and drive, Mydei squinting in the dark until he can see a spark of light. Cipher flags them down with a small flare, burning blue in the night. "There," Mydei says. His voice is rough. "To the right." Anaxa slows to a stop, and they pick Cipher back up. She's pale and covered in red blood and sweat, but she’s grinning as she stomps out the flare and climbs into the car.

"My in-ear broke," she says, buckling in. She passes Mydei's gun back with shaking hands, the proof that she’s not half as unruffled as she seems. "How's Tribbie's car?"

"Good," Anaxa says. "It was just those three cars following. She’s got Phainon and that woman and they’re heading home."

"Thank the Titans," Cipher sighs, splaying in her seat. For a long while, they all just breathe. Anaxa drives them home.

"How's the kid?” he asks. "Still knocked out?"

Mydei looks over. Castorice's mouth is slack, eyes shut. She's still thin and dirty and drugged, blood on her clothes, but her chest rises and falls softly. "Yeah," Mydei confirms.

"Oh, she’s gonna hate me when she wakes up," Cipher says, turning awkwardly again. Her breath has calmed, expression smoothed out as she studies Castorice. One of her ears flicks, blood caught in her fur. “What a princess,” she murmurs, propping her chin on her arms. "What was her name? She told you, didn’t she? Before I had to play villain?”

Castorice's head falls against the window, neck uncomfortably bent. It's a wonder she didn't wake up through all the gunfire and swerving. It must’ve been a strong sedative. The sound of her cries echoes in Mydei’s head, over and over.

"Castorice," he says. "Her name is Castorice."

They get home without issue. Tribbie's group gets back first; Aglaea is already passed out in bed, and Phainon waits for them in the living room. Cipher retreats to bathe. Castorice doesn't wake. Mydei has to carry her up. There’s nowhere for her to stay, so Mydei puts her in his own bed for the night. He'll sleep on the couch, and they'll figure out something more permanent in the morning. Assuming Castorice wants to stay with them at all.

She's still all dirty. Mydei just washed his sheets. He leaves a glass of water on the nightstand and steals one of the pillows.

Phainon is on the couch when he comes back out. He's changed his clothes and washed off the blood, but Mydei doesn't think he showered. His hair isn’t wet. It's too late for that. He's too tired. Once the adrenaline runs out, they all crash, left with nothing but this bone-deep exhaustion from a job well done. Mydei sits down next to him. Silently, Phainon tips into his shoulder.

"How was that?" he asks. "Pretty good job, huh?”

"We all almost died,” Mydei says. All it earns him is a hum. He looks at Phainon. His closed eyes, his smushed cheek. He’s warm now, injured hand freshly bandaged in his lap. “How’s your hand?”

“Fine,” Phainon answers. His eyes are still closed. Maybe he’s falling asleep. He’s quiet for a little while. “I get why she’s so afraid of touching people,” he adds after a while. “It might’ve been the worst pain of my life.”

“And yet you were so insistent on saving her,” Mydei murmurs. He leans his cheek against Phainon’s hair. Their thighs press. One of Phainon’s ankles curls around his.

“We’re all strays, Mydeimos,” he says, echoing his words from before. A pause, a breath. The lights flicker, and he shifts further against Mydei’s side. Careful, Mydei slips an arm around his back. “She reminded me of you, a little bit.”

Mydei scoffs. “I didn’t cry and curl up like that.”

“No,” Phainon chuckles. His good hand crawls over their thighs, pinky hooking Mydei’s until he turns his hand up and their fingers slot together. Wound together like this, it’s hard to tell whose warmth is whose. They need to talk, but this is good enough, isn’t it? We’re okay, it says. Nothing needs to change. “You only knew how to hurt people, but… you didn’t want to. I think she’s like that too.”

“Those are some big assumptions to make about someone you’ve only just met.”

Phainon hums softly, tips his face up to look at Mydei, close enough to share breath, eyes clear blue and warmer than they ought to be. “Maybe.” A pause, their eyes on each other. “I’m glad you could be there.”

“I barely did anything.”

“No,” Phainon says, and skims his injured fingers along Mydei’s jaw. He leans in for a kiss, just once, just softly. His mouth is warmer than the rest of him. He tastes like mint, and his eyes take a while to open after he pulls away. "You did plenty."

Mydei kisses him again, just a press of lips. He feels Phainon’s exhale against him, sucks softly on his bottom lip. They’re both too exhausted for anything more than this. He pulls back, and Phainon settles back against him, squeezing their joined hands.

They're quiet for a little while. This is familiar. They do this a lot, after every mission. Sometimes Aglaea and Cipher will join them too, and the four of them will sit and talk until they're too tired for even that. So Mydei always feels like family, even if he doesn’t get to go on the missions with them.

"I'm glad we got Aglaea back,” Phainon murmurs.

"Me too."

Phainon sighs softly. “Do you think Castorice will want to stay?” he asks.

"Depends." It isn’t much of an answer, but Mydei doesn’t know. She’d been so scared, and then Cipher had to hit her with a tranquilizer. She’ll wake up safe and unharmed, but Mydei can’t imagine this building a good foundation for trust. "We’ll find out in the morning, I guess.”

“In the morning,” Phainon repeats. He’s a soft creature at night. Mydei is too. Too tired to fight him, to argue, to bicker. There’s just this. Sturdy weight and body heat. The bloody smell of him. “Were you going to sleep out here?”

“Yeah,” Mydei whispers.

“Come to my room,” Phainon says. “It’s a squeeze, but I don’t mind.” His bed is only a twin. They’ve packed into it together before, but Mydei doesn’t like to be presumptuous. Not when neither of them is quite sure what exactly this is.

“Alright,” Mydei says. He can’t think of a reason to protest. Phainon is warm. He’s so tired. Together, they stand and drag their feet to Phainon’s room. When they crawl under the covers, side by side, Mydei is out like a light.

In the morning, Castorice is gone.

Mydei's back in the dungeon. He goes on three more missions within the next six months while everyone else probably goes on a dozen or more. Seven more, within the year. More than one every other month. It might be the best ratio he’s ever had, which is saying something. The Cleaners have been busy, and he’s needed more and more. He feels more productive, more useful, more like part of the team, even if he still has to stay back more often than not.

That’s what happens today. Another mission where Mydei isn’t needed. Aglaea is the brains, Phainon the brawn, Cipher the shadows. It's fine. He could have come in the getaway car if he wanted, but he hates that more than this. Instead, he cleans up their flat a little, cooks himself dinner, and curls up on the couch to watch a movie. Maybe he should look into adopting a pet. Maybe a dog so he has a reason to go outside. Phainon would probably try to talk him into getting a cat instead. Cipher might too. He doesn’t think Aglaea would care either way.

A cat, then. A cat would probably be best, just so Phainon is happy. Cipher too.

Mydei is home alone watching a movie in his shared four-bedroom flat when there's a knock on the door. A delivery, maybe. Cipher is known to order more things than she needs and hoard them in her room. He isn’t sure, so he pauses the movie and gets up. He opens the door.

There's a girl in the hallway, gloved hands clasped in front of her, gaze climbing the door frame before it lands on Mydei. Her hair is long enough to reach her knees, soft pink, neatly combed, and styled into twin ponytails. The sweater she wears covers her practically up to the jaw. "Hello."

"Hi," Mydei says. "It's been a while."

"There are people after me," Castorice says, awkwardly smiling. She's a far cry from the distressed, drugged-up creature she'd been a year ago. "I don't have many options, but… turn me away, if it’s a bother."

Mydei looks at her a little longer. The way her gaze stubbornly avoids his. The way her fingers are tangled tight in front of her. The way there isn't a single inch of exposed skin below her head. It's the middle of summer.

"Come in," Mydei tells her, backing out of the doorway. "I'm watching a movie. I can restart it, if you want."

△

Castorice has this way of sitting quietly, body as small as possible. They sit next to each other on the couch, but it doesn't really feel like it, with how much space she gives Mydei. She's still wearing her gloves and her turtleneck and long pants and socks. Mydei is in shorts and a tank top. Barefoot. The movie he'd been watching plays on in the silence. Castorice hasn't said a word.

"You can take the gloves off," Mydei says. They keep the flat kind of warm in the summer to save on the energy bill. Cold in the winter too. "Roll up your sleeves or whatever; I know it's hot as hell in here."

"Thank you," Castorice says, and does no such thing. Mydei watches her from the corner of his eye. The way she sits small and stiff. She's only pretending to watch the movie, same as he is. The smallest sound or movement makes her curl in on herself. Mydei sucks in a breath.

"I'm the only one home tonight," he says. "The others are out on a mission and probably won't be back until way later." Castorice doesn't look at him. Mydei plays with his own fingers and adds, because his gut is twisting with Titans know what, "You're not at risk of hurting anyone."

Castorice's breath stills before she picks it back up. She doesn't display any other reaction. After a long moment, quietly, carefully, she peels her gloves off one by one. She sets them on her knees and folds her bare, slender hands in her lap like she doesn't know what to do with them. Mydei said that to make her comfortable. Somehow, she seems even less so.

"Castorice"

She looks at him and looks horribly out of place, like she doesn't think she belongs here, or anywhere at all, and Mydei doesn’t have a weakness for strays, not the way the rest of them do, but he knows what that feels like. To be afraid of the world, but mostly your own hands. To not have a soul to trust on the entire planet.

“I don’t know if I ever got your name,” she says softly. “Or I must’ve forgotten, what with…” She doesn’t mention the drugging, or the tranquilizer, or the way she left in the morning. Who knows how much of it she remembers, regardless.

“Mydei,” he tells her. “How much do you remember?”

The way she shrunk back like she does now. The way she tried so hard to keep them from touching her, pleading and begging them not to. The way they did anyway, and then knocked her out. She might have woken up safe and sound, but she must be desperate to come back here.

Castorice tucks her hands between her thighs like she wants to hide all her bare skin. She’s so good at shrinking she could probably disappear if she tried. “Enough,” she answers.

“Then you know that you can’t hurt me,” Mydei tells her. “I carried you out of there, and I’m just fine. You can relax.”

Castorice hesitates. "I know,” she agrees.

Something about her body language, the set of her expression. "You think it was a fluke,” Mydei notes. He cocks his head when she doesn’t reply. "You were drugged as hell, do you remember that part?”

"Why aren't you on the mission with the rest of your group?" Castorice asks. It feels random. It feels like a diversion.

Mydei waves her off. "I'm not useful the way the rest of them are," he says. "Do you remember?"

"What do you mean you're not useful? You're immune to things; isn't that one of the best powers you could have for your... job?"'

Job. That's almost funny. "Castorice."

Castorice takes a breath. "Yes,” she says. “I remember.”

The movie drones on. Neither of them is pretending to watch it anymore. Mydei's already seen this part anyway. He studies her. "Why are you here,” he asks.

Castorice's lips part. She wets them, avoiding eye contact. Her voice is soft and small when she speaks. "I had nowhere else to go."

"You said people are after you."

"Yes."

"Is it the Cleaners?" They’re after all of them. If you bleed gold, if you have a power, the Cleaners want you gone, and the cops won’t bother to do anything about it.

Castorice doesn’t answer, but the way she tenses up is as good as a yes. Mydei goes quiet, just thinking. A long moment passes. Finally, she speaks. "I've heard people say that touching me is the worst pain they've experienced in their life." She pauses, but Mydei doesn't interrupt her. Phainon said that too. "Skin to skin is like… It’ll melt the skin off your hand if you touch me long enough. Even through clothes... You saw your friend's hand. That's why I—"

Phainon’s fingers are still scarred faintly, a year later. "They want to use you as a weapon," Mydei realizes.

"Have been," Castorice corrects. A beat. "Or… A torture device. Not really a weapon."

"Why were you there, that day?"

"I was being sold off," Castorice says, "to someone else who wanted to..."

Mydei looks at her. Clothing covering her head to toe. Bare hands tangled in her lap. "Would you trust me for a second?”

"I don't know you at all."

"But you came here," Mydei says, pausing the TV. The silence between them rings without the movie as background noise. "You're scared and you have nowhere to go. You probably can't trust a single person on this earth, but you came here, and that has to count for something." Silence. Castorice only looks at him. Slowly, Mydei holds a hand out, palm up, fingers open. She eyes it warily. "Take my hand."

"I think it's best if I don't."

"I won't make you," Mydei tells her. "But you won’t hurt me if you do, and it might be nice to know that when you’re not drugged to hell.”

She frowns. A moment passes, and Mydei starts to withdraw his hand.

"Wait." Castorice wets her lips. Slowly, she reaches out, pausing close, but not enough to touch. She looks like she regrets it as soon as she does. Mydei meets her eyes and counts to six. He takes Castorice's hand in his.

Instantly, she flinches, shivers, pulls her hand free, tucking it with the other between her thighs. She looks shaken, and Mydei opens his palms. Smooth, pale, skin. A tiny scar from where he’d cut himself while cooking, but no burns, no blood. "Doesn't hurt a bit," he says. Castorice stares at his hand for a while longer, and then she clears her throat.

"Your... organization," she says, "do you have a leader?"

Mydei drops his hands into his lap, settling more comfortably on the couch. "Kind of?" he tries. They consider Aglaea their leader, but she doesn’t call herself that. "We're really just a group of dumbasses.”

"And yet…" Castorice pauses. "You were involved in... whatever that was, that night. And your friends are out on a 'mission.'"

"Dumbasses who do stuff to make ends meet," Mydei amends.

"Stuff," Castorice repeats.

"Dangerous and illegal stuff," Mydei offers. "Vigilante shit. We fight the Cleaners. I'm sure you've seen how effective the police are around here." Quietly, Castorice nods. She would know better than anyone. Who knows how long she'd been trafficked and used as a weapon.

"Hey," he says instead, "I don't know what you were looking for when you came here, but we take people in all the time. You can stay, if you want. You could have stayed back then."

Castorice thinks about this for a long time, staring into her lap. "You'd be surprised," she says, "by how many times I've heard that."

"Ah." Mydei gets that too. That day in the dirt, Phainon pinning him down and letting him go, he hadn’t understood what they wanted from him either. He hadn’t believed he could trust them. So he ran, and the next time he saw them, he lost the fight and was offered a place to stay. He stands up and stretches. “Think on it for a bit, then. I’ll give you money for a hotel and Aglaea’s number. Come back if you want, or don’t.”

Castorice hesitates. “...Aglaea?”

"Our leader, kind of. You asked about her."

Castorice is silent. She plays with her gloves in her lap and then pulls them back on. "Okay," she says after a moment. Again, quieter, "Okay."

Mydei finds his wallet. There's two hundred dollars in it. Enough for a hotel and whatever else Castorice might need. Mydei doesn't know how she's been living up until now. He takes all of the money and drops it in her lap. She barely even looks at it before she says, "That's too much."

Two hundred dollars. Too much for a cheap hotel and a gas station meal, sure. "It's expensive around here," Mydei lies. She looks at him for a long moment before she splits the cash in half and sets the extra on the coffee table. Quietly, she stands, and then she leaves like that. Like the wind.

Dressed head to toe in the middle of summer, a hundred dollars in her pocket.

Phainon, Cipher, and Aglaea come home late. They bring cuts and bruises with them, but they say the mission went about as well as it could have. They're still alive, and that's enough.

Phainon comes to Mydei with a bruise under his shoulder blade. He says he'd been hit with a pipe, and though he'd heard it coming, he wasn't fast enough to dodge. His knuckles are busted too. He punched a wall instead of a person and used a little too much force. His strength has been presented for years now, but he still forgets it sometimes.

He peels off his shirt in the bathroom for Mydei to put ointment on his back, the bruise already dark and discolored.

“You’re too reckless,” Mydei tells him. “Why didn’t you go to Hyacine?”

“It’s not that bad,” Phainon protests, but he winces as Mydei’s fingers skim the injury to rub the ointment in. “I’m pretty sturdy.”

Mydei snorts and steps back, twisting the cap back onto the tube of ointment. “Sure,” he says, and Phainon turns around so they’re face to face, packed tight into this tiny bathroom. He’s smiling a little. There’s always this gnawing feeling in the back of his mind that never eases until he sees Phainon safe after a job.

“I am!” Phainon insists, blue eyed and messy haired and bare chested. Mydei takes his injured hand, dried and scabbed now, and pulls it to the sink to wash. “You’ve tested it yourself.”

“You’ve got fucking super strength and somehow you still lose to me sometimes,” Mydei chuckles. He’s gentle as he rubs away the crusted gold blood under the faucet, but Phainon still hisses through his teeth. “So sturdy,” he teases. Phainon flicks a bit of water at him.

“Shut up, that hand’s been hurting for hours.”

“Maybe don’t punch walls, then.” The faucet squeaks as Mydei shuts it off. He towel dries Phainon’s hand and feels along his bones to make sure they’re all in place, gaze tipped down between them.

“Nothing’s broken,” Phainon says softly. His breath ruffles Mydei’s hair. His hand flexes demonstratively in Mydei’s. “Just sore.”

So Mydei rubs ointment into his knuckles too and wraps his hand in white bandages. It’s the same hand with the shiny scar tissue from Castorice. Phainon is always hurting his hands. They’re rough with callouses and crooked from broken fingers not set correctly. Sometimes his body can’t keep up with how strong he is.

“Try not to use this, for a while,” Mydei says, securing the edge of the bandage. “Hyacine will kick your ass if you make it worse.”

“Yeah, yeah,” Phainon murmurs. The fingers of his good hand skim Mydei’s waist. They look at each other. His smile is soft, beckoning. “Sorry.”

“Stop getting hurt, and you won’t have to apologize,” Mydei shoots back. But he steps closer, he always does. Phainon lets him cage him in against the counter, tips their mouths together first. He tastes a bit like blood. Mydei kisses him long and slow, draws back only enough to lean their foreheads together.

“You should pester Aglaea about coming on more missions,” Phainon whispers. He knows best how restless Mydei gets. He’s been going on more and more missions lately, but it still isn’t enough. He still can’t fight that useless feeling, but he never protests, never asks to be made part of the plan. It really would be as easy as that.

“I know,” he says. Phainon kisses his cheek this time, cupping the back of his neck. There’s the scratch of bandages against skin. He uses his hurt hand for this. “Phainon.”

“I want you by my side,” Phainon murmurs, kissing a little higher up his cheekbone. “I’ll ask for you, if you want.”

“Don’t fight my battles for me.”

“Alright,” Phainon says softly. He pulls back just a bit. “Sleep in my bed tonight?”

“Yeah,” Mydei says. “Yeah, I’ll come.” So they sleep in the same bed that night. Packed just a bit too tight. It’s too warm under the blankets, and Phainon drools on his shoulder. They still don’t talk about it. They do this and they kiss but they don’t talk about it, but titans be damned if Mydei isn’t home.

In the morning, Castorice doesn't come. They wake up late and have breakfast. Mydei waits until noon before he goes grocery shopping, just in case. He drags Cipher with him, so she won't be alone. Cipher often spirals if she's left alone after a job. Aglaea usually handles it, but Mydei doesn’t mind bringing her today. The company is nice. He just has to keep an eye out to make sure she doesn’t steal anything.

She complains a bit as they pick out fruit. He won’t let her get six different flavors of ice cream. When he catches her about to slip away, probably to steal, he grabs her by the hood the way one might scruff a housecat. She doesn’t take kindly to this, but he doesn’t particularly care.

His thoughts turn back to Castorice. Over and over, he sees the look in her eyes. It isn't his business. It shouldn't matter to him. He wishes he could forget like he did a year ago, but he can't. Not this time. Phainon’s soft spot for strays must be rubbing off on him.

They go home. Phainon is on lunch duty. None of them are in the mood to go out again today. Mydei sits with Cipher and Aglaea on the couch as they wait for Phainon to concoct something hopefully edible from the ingredients Mydei bought. They watch something on the TV. There's no knock on the door throughout the rest of the day. By the time they go to bed, there's no sign of Castorice coming back. No sign she was ever here at all.

"Do you want the couch?" Mydei asks, reaching for Phainon’s hand and pulling him a few feet down the hallway to the coat closet, stuffed with extra blankets and pillows.

"That's..." Castorice goes quiet. She takes the blankets Phainon holds out to her, the pillow Mydei does. She’s careful not to touch them, and Mydei studies her expression. "Thank you," she says, a bit baffled, swiftly breaking eye contact, stepping back so they aren't so close, letting them lead the way into the living room. She sits gingerly on the couch, pulling her legs up, setting the pillow behind her and stacking the blankets on her lap.

"What you asked, earlier," Mydei says. Castorice looks up at him, face carefully blank. "Were you serious?"

Castorice swallows visibly and looks away again. Her gloved fingers twist in her lap. "And what about you? Were you serious?"

He’d felt that way too, wondered why anyone would want a half-feral, half-drowned kid as a friend and a part of the family. But they did, and here he is, with a purpose and people who love him, even if it comes with a bit of danger. He’s not sure he’d like a mundane life anyway. Once, there was a time when that was all he wished for.

He sits on the opposite end of the couch, giving her plenty of space, dragging Phainon along with him. “Yes,” he says, “I was.”

“I…” Phainon hesitates, wetting his lips and glancing at Mydei before he continues speaking. “I don’t know what all Mydei has told you about us, but… We’re all like you, in a way. My house burned down and killed my whole family, and I was on the streets for a few months before Aglaea found me. I wasn’t sure about staying either, but… we’re good people. Or, I like to think so.” He laughs weakly, scrubs the back of his neck. “I meant what I said earlier, too. About being a friend, if you want that. I can’t speak for everyone else, but I highly doubt any of them would say no.”

“If you want a place,” Mydei says softly.

“I owe you all a lot already,” Castorice murmurs, hugging one of the blankets close to her chest. Her lower lip wobbles, chin dimpling. “I just don’t want to hurt anyone anymore.”

“No one here will make you,” Mydei promises her again, and waits. The offer is there; Castorice just needs to take it. A hard choice, he knows, to someone so scarred and scared of trusting.

"Okay." Castorice nods once, swallows. “I want to believe you. You’ve all been nothing but kind to me.”

“We know how hard it is to believe in something like this, trust me,” Phainon says. He laughs a little, nostalgic, knuckles brushing Mydei’s thigh until their hands twine together. “You can take a year to decide, if you need. Two. You have our numbers; feel free to come and go as much as you want.”

Castorice looks conflicted at this too. She won’t want to be on the run anymore. She must be tired of it, bone weary to the point of breaking down, too exhausted to keep being afraid. Starved of safety. Mydei’s been there too.

The floorboards creak as Aglaea comes down the hallway, dressed in a yellow nightgown that buttons up the front. “Lovely to have a visitor,” she says, taking a seat in one of the armchairs beside the couch. Her hair still looks perfect, even this late. They must’ve woken her, despite how hushed they’ve been. “Castorice, yes? It’s a pleasure to finally meet you in person.”

At her arrival, Castorice looks terribly embarrassed. She stands and bows at the waist, lengthy ponytails slipping over her shoulder and just about brushing the floor. “I apologize if we woke you up,” she says helplessly. “I only meant to…”

“Relax,” Aglaea says, smiling a bit. She has a cold, calculating smile, but it seems that even she’s trying to soften herself now. Slowly, Castorice sits back down.

“I’m happy to arrange for your extended stay,” Aglaea continues after a moment. “How long that’s for, whether just a week or permanently is up to you. Unfortunately, we can’t just house you for free.” She pauses, and Castorice stiffens. “Mission work is how most of us earn our keep, but I understand if that’s undesirable to you. Do you sew, perhaps? Or are you handy with tools? There are a number of things that need mending around here, but it can be a bit difficult to explain certain things around here to hired help.”

“I…” Castorice opens her mouth, closes it. “Yes, I… Can help with those kinds of things, but… Surely a bit of work like that isn’t enough to pay for rent or… whatever else.”

Aglaea hums, rotating her ankle, propping her cheek on her fist as she considers. “Yes… Perhaps not. I can inquire with Tribios about finding other work for you. Perhaps you’d like to assist Hyacine in concocting medicines and preparing things in her infirmary?”

Castorice squirms. “I don’t believe I’m particularly suitable for that kind of work.”

“And why not?” Aglaea asks. “It’s not as if you can cause pain through inanimate objects, can you? A healing salve by your hand would be the same as one by Hyacine’s, assuming you use the proper ingredients.”

Phainon’s hand tightens around Mydei’s. He’s invested in this, just like he’d been that first day. Mydei has to admit that he is too.

“I suppose so,” Castorice admits, though she seems reluctant to believe it.

Aglaea waves her hand. “Think on it. There’s no rush to decide. We can search for more options if none of those appeal to you.”

“I…” Castorice’s eyes look wet. She opens her mouth to speak when there’s a groan from down the hall. This time it’s Cipher, coming out in a t-shirt and money printed pajama pants with perhaps the worst bedhead Mydei has seen on a person. She has Bubbles tucked happily in her arms, though she’s making a disgruntled face as she comes to join them.

“What infernal racket,” she complains, “I’m no Lady Goldweaver, but a cat’s ears are sensitive too, alright? What’s so important that you have to talk about it in the middle of the night?”

On her shoulder, Bubbles meows in agreement. When she notices them all staring, she scratches him on the head and adds, “What? He sleeps in my room now.”

Castorice just stares. Maybe she remembers Cipher drugging her, maybe she doesn’t, but she seems a bit horrified by the catgirl’s appearance. “Hello, Princess No-touchy,” Cipher says to her. “It’s wonderful to properly meet you, but some of us need our rest. Can I fluff your pillow so you can sleep extra cozy?”

“Cifera,” Aglaea admonishes. Cipher makes a petulant sound.

“Yeah, yeah, sorry,” she says, and falls into the other armchair. Bubbles settles in her lap, and Mydei can hear him purring, even from here. It’s the strangest, most sickening betrayal he’s ever experienced. She rubs circles into his ears and turns back to Castorice. “So. You staying?”

“I…”

“Please say yes,” Cipher tells her. “I’m around too many boys all the time. And Aglaea is mean, so she doesn’t count.”

Castorice looks at Mydei now, absolutely helpless, and he can’t stop the laugh that bursts out of him. Maybe he’s just tired, but what the fuck? What a day. At his side, Phainon laughs too, and then they’re all kind of laughing, even Castorice, though hers is awkward and nervous. The effort is there. Mydei thinks she’ll fit right in.

△

In the end, Castorice decides to stay, though she decides to leave for tonight, if only for fear that Bubbles might get curious about her while she’s sleeping and hurt himself. So Cipher and Aglaea go back to bed, and Mydei and Phainon walk her to the door.

"Goodnight, then," Mydei tells her, and she says it back, bowing her head politely.

“Can I count you as a friend?” Phainon asks, and her eyes widen a bit as she turns to him, inhaling.

“Friends,” she breathes.

“Friends,” Phainon echoes back, smiling like some goddamn sun.

“It might be nice to have some, if you’re staying,” Mydei points out.

She smiles, a small, hesitant thing, and nods. “Friends,” she agrees, testing the feel of it in her mouth, like it’s a foreign thing to her. And maybe it is, but it doesn’t have to be. After a breath, Mydei holds out a hand.

“Should we shake on it?” he asks, and Castorice just stares at his hand like it's some kind of wild animal. He makes to lower it. “We don’t have to, if you don’t want.”

“No, I…” Her fingers twitch. “It might be nice,” she says, as Mydei had. Gingerly, she reaches out, then pauses before their hands can come in contact. "What if it stops working?" she croaks. “I don’t want—”

“My power is like yours,” Mydei explains. “It doesn’t just turn off and on. If it didn’t hurt the first time, it won’t hurt now.”

"Okay," Castorice says, and tentatively clasps his hand. Her grip is loose and uncertain, still gloved, the fabric a bit damp with cold sweat. She holds her breath as they shake once, and then she pulls her hand back, folding it toward her body and clearing her throat. It must be strange, scary, touching without consequence, but Mydei will let her take that at her own pace, if she decides she wants to.

“There,” he says simply. “It’s official.”

"Friends," Castorice says once more, like a broken record. She smiles a little. Mydei tries to smile back, wonders if it looks weird on his face.

“Maybe I’ll get one of those plastic mannequin hands,” Phainon interjects, “that way I can shake your hand too.”

Miraculously, this makes her laugh. A real, genuine laugh, high and girlish. Her smile crinkles her eyes. “Sure,” she says, “then you can all take turns shaking my hand, just so we can make it official.” Her voice is watery.

There’s a good chance she’ll cry when she returns to her own temporary home. Maybe not from sadness. Mydei doesn’t comment.

“Give us a few more days, and we’ll take care of the Cleaners for you too,” Phainon tells her. “We’ve been looking for a good lead on them for a long time. And then you won’t have much to be afraid of anymore.”

She looks tired, grateful. Mydei will be going on that mission too. Maybe he should be afraid, but he’s just… excited. Glad he’ll be useful, glad he can be there to have everyone else’s backs, glad to have the chance to do something good, for all the Castorices of the world.

“Thank you,” she says, voice breaking, now. Mydei could offer to hug her, but he won’t. Not for a long time, until he’s sure she’s ready for that. “Stay safe, please. They’re dangerous.”

“Aglaea and Anaxa came up with a plan,” Phainon tells her. “The plan never goes south when those two manage to get along long enough to work together.”

“Good,” she says, and turns halfway to the door. A brief pause, she looks between them. “I’ll… see you?”

“Of course,” Phainon says, easy as breathing, like that’s the most obvious thing in the world. Mydei envies the way he can make anyone feel comfortable.

“You will,” he agrees, and tries to smile again. Castorice smiles back, undoes the lock on the door, hand lingering on the knob.

“Goodnight,” she says again.

“Goodnight,” they echo back, and when the door shuts between them, it isn’t for long. She'll be back, Mydei knows. Strays calls to strays.
